_meta.indication: ZAVZPRET is indicated for the acute treatment of migraine with or without aura in adults; it is not indicated for preventive treatment of migraine.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 1 (BHV3500-301), a Phase 3 trial evaluating the 10 mg dose
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, outpatient trial; patients randomized 1:1 to a single 10 mg intranasal zavegepant dose or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adults age ≥18 years with at least a one-year history of migraine with or without aura, no more than 8 moderate/severe migraine attacks per month, treating a migraine of moderate to severe headache pain intensity
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints of pain freedom and most bothersome symptom (MBS) freedom at 2 hours after a single dose
pivotal_trials.result: Pain freedom at 2 hours: 23.6% (147/623) vs 14.9% (96/646) placebo, difference 8.8%, p<0.001; MBS freedom at 2 hours: 39.6% (247/623) vs 31.1% (201/646), difference 8.7%, p=0.001

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, dose-ranging study; patients randomized 1:1:1:1 to a single dose of zavegepant 5 mg, 10 mg, or 20 mg or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with migraine treating a migraine attack of moderate to severe pain intensity
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints of pain freedom and most bothersome symptom (MBS) freedom at 2 hours after a single dose
pivotal_trials.n: n=391 (ZAVZPRET 10 mg) and n=401 (placebo) in the 10 mg comparison
pivotal_trials.result: Pain freedom at 2 hours: 22.5% (88/391) vs 15.5% (62/401) placebo, difference 7.0%, p=0.011; MBS freedom at 2 hours: 41.9% (164/391) vs 33.7% (135/401), difference 8.3%, p=0.016

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (at least 2% and greater than placebo): taste disorders (18% vs 4% placebo), nausea (4% vs 1%), nasal discomfort (3% vs 1%), and vomiting (2% vs <1%). Hypersensitivity, including facial swelling and urticaria, occurred in less than 1% of treated patients.
target_moa: Zavegepant is a calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor antagonist; it is the first intranasally administered CGRP receptor antagonist reviewed by FDA.
modality: Small molecule (zavegepant hydrochloride), delivered as an intranasal spray

rems.type: DRM determined that a REMS is not needed to ensure the benefits of zavegepant outweigh its risks.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the applicant provided substantial evidence of effectiveness from two adequate and well-controlled studies and the safety profile was deemed acceptable.

basis.text: The application was reviewed under Standard (not Priority) review.

requirement.text: 4408-5: Prospective pregnancy exposure registry cohort analyses in the U.S. comparing maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women with migraine exposed to zavegepant during pregnancy with two unexposed control populations.

citations.quote: 4408-5 Prospective pregnancy exposure registry cohort analyses in the United States that compare the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women with migraine exposed to zavegepant during pregnancy with two unexposed control populations: one consisting of women with migraine who have not been exposed to zavegepant before or during pregnancy, and the other consisting of women without migraine. The registry will identify and record pregnancy complications, major and minor congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, elective terminations, preterm births, small-for-gestational-age births, and any other adverse outcomes, including postnatal growth and development. Outcomes will be assessed throughout pregnancy. Infant outcomes, including effects on postnatal growth and development, will be assessed through at least the first year of life.

requirement.text: 4408-6: A pregnancy outcomes study using a different design than PMR 4408-5 (e.g., retrospective cohort using claims/EMR data or a case-control study) to assess pregnancy complications, major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, and small-for-gestational-age births in women exposed to zavegepant during pregnancy versus an unexposed control population.
